Balance block

Anatomy

₴3,240

Available to withdraw

  1. 1.dr-balanceThe block: a figure over the line that names it, 4 apart. As --card it turns on its side inside a green card, 341 × 84, padding 20 / 16 (16 / 16 below 390 wide), radius 16, no shadow; glyph and body are 12 apart.
  2. 2.dr-balance__glyphA 44 × 44 square plate, radius 13, --bg-accent-tint, with a 22px coin stack inside it. Its 44 is the body's own height (22 + 4 + 18), so glyph and text share a top and a bottom edge.
  3. 3.dr-numberThe figure, 700 with tabular figures and line-height 1, so money lines up digit under digit. Inside .dr-balance it takes the display size, 22, in place of the number step's 20.
  4. 4.dr-note--flushThe caption, 12 regular at line-height 1.5 (18), set left instead of the note's default centre.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Balance block.

States

No state of its own: the block shows a figure and the line that names it, and nothing in it takes focus.

When to use

A balance block is the headline figure of a screen and the line that names it: the amount being paid on payment, the money available on wallet and withdraw, the balance below the minimum on wallet-empty, the overall rating on ratings. It replaces the grayscale .amount at 34/600, a size outside the ten steps and an ink outside the palette. A balance is the definition of a figure the user verifies, so it is always .dr-number, tabular.

The two filled versions are green cards that sit in the page like any other card, with no shadow. Their cost is recorded: on wallet the card alone is 8.82% of the frame and, with the floating action, the screen's solid green reaches 11.32% against the ~5% ceiling, a departure the designer was shown and kept. The patterns are the product's one decoration, taken on her word.

The caption names what the figure is, in the user's words: Available to withdraw, the service and route on payment. Money out is Withdraw; a figure is stated, never celebrated.
